issues: All six views were zooms of the generic small-type FakeDashboard on light grey with indigo, so however fast the cuts, you couldn't tell what the product was
The picture was dead: nothing moved between cuts, so the acceleration existed only in the edit
After the last cut back to the wide there was no payoff; the accelerating approach led nowhere
In the wide shot type was 10-14px, barely readable even in the 2.6x close-up
changes: Ember look: the product is now a race-telemetry wall, Pitwall, with a 260px speed readout, gear and shift lights, a car dot running the track map, a 108px lap delta, sector times and throttle/brake traces, all readable in the wide
The content is live: the car keeps running, speed climbs to 312 and the delta keeps growing, so the six hard cuts are six cameras on the same moment
The cuts tell a story: wide, track map, speed, delta, throttle trace, then a chase close-up locked to the car; intervals stay 16/12/8/6/4 and the in-shot push speeds up each segment
After the final cut back to the wide, a 'FASTEST LAP 1:31.204' badge springs in 4f later and S3 lights as the best sector, landing the conclusion; the hold is now 45f
Cut-frame click: one frame at +6% brightness with a 6% warm-white layer, and each new view settles 1.03 to 1 over 4f; zoom uses CSS zoom so the 3.4x close-up stays sharp
